title: The Long Road To Nowhere
title_history: Began as a blog (Diary of an Apprentice), became Diary of a Chef, then widened into a life-long memoir. 'The Long Road To Nowhere' was the original first chapter's title; it broke the chapter naming convention and was promoted to book title, where it fits the road travelled.
language_note: Australian/NZ English spelling. Output language for all skill responses.
target_reader: Someone struggling who believes life won't change — and Madz, one day.
source_of_truth: GitHub techcorp-DevApps/memoir. CLAUDE.md §5–6 authoritative for canon; context/ and planning/ govern voice and structure. This config summarises and points; it never overrides those files.

author_profile.who_they_are: Bosco. Career chef, from apprentice to award-winning chef, teacher, leader and parent, across New Zealand and Australia. Reached the kitchen through an unconventional youth: father's death at 11, foster care, on his own around 15, left school at 13, crime and heavy drug use, sentenced at 19 (18 charges, concurrent). Then roughly three years in a NZ vineyard kitchen under Chef (Geoffrey Welham), Chef de Cuisine at 24, turned around a failing 150-cover bistro, later Melbourne Italian fine dining.
author_profile.authority: Lived all of it. Commercial-kitchen experience from the pass and the rail, not TV or foodie culture, plus a life that shows what in-the-moment decisions cost the future self.
author_profile.relationship_with_subject: Witness first, expert second. Inside each moment and also the adult looking back with hindsight. The ChefTips carry the expert layer.
author_profile.reader_relationship: Conversation, with some teaching. Direct 'you' address. Kitchen people should recognise themselves, and outsiders get dragged into the kitchen. Provokes the reader's own 'how did I get here?'
author_profile.emotional_core: Integrity, loyalty, honesty and respect never change. What changes is the understanding of how they are applied, given and expected, which life only supplies once it has been lived. 00_ONE_THING_LED_TO_ANOTHER establishes this: decisions in the moment rarely consider their future impact.
the_risk: His father's death at 11 and its aftermath, never spoken about in the family. Ma will read it and still blames herself. Likely to solidify what he has always said on the matter.
The hardest: the death of his son Jackson at age 7, in his arms (severe asthma attack). Only one piece exists so far, 'TheUniverse', a brief snapshot of the evening before.
handling_rules: B30 (binding): no career chapter foreshadows Jackson's death. That material sits after §23 closes the ChefTip ladder.
Father and Jackson chapters are interview-first. Nothing is drafted until the author has told it his way, at his pace.
Composites and disguises per CLAUDE.md §5 (e.g. Marco composite stays undisclosed).
author_profile.key_relationships: Ma, Steven/CJ (brother), father ('the old man'), Jackson (son), Madison (daughter), Chef/Geoffrey Welham, Fat Sam, Dave, Si, Ivian; bistro brigade Praveen, Sonny, Jen. Full registry: CLAUDE.md §5 and context/canon.md.

preset_digest: Biography / narrative non-fiction (memoir). Identity: a true life read through the author's interpretation. Vocabulary: central claim → the interpretation; chapter goal → revelatory moment; scene → reconstructed moment; character arc → the subject's trajectory. Demolish vectors in order: evidence, alternative interpretation, selection bias, authorial intrusion, presentism, gaps (reconstruction vs documented fact). Write pattern: the scene (concrete, sourced, puts the reader in the room) → the context → the significance. Project overrides: CLAUDE.md voice rules, ChefTip and Reflective Memory patterns, canon, and B30 take precedence.

book_profile.premise: Most people believe their life is shaped by big, deliberate choices. The truth is that one thing leads to another, and decisions made in the moment, with no thought for the future self, build the road. Integrity, loyalty, honesty and respect hold steady the whole way, but you only learn how to apply them by living.
book_profile.premise_extended: This is not just a story about kitchens, careers, mistakes, or second chances. It is a reflection on the people, choices, challenges, and moments that shape who we become—or, more importantly, who I have become. From a difficult and uncertain beginning, the story moves through the intensity of professional kitchens, personal battles, unexpected friendships, and the pursuit of something better. Honest, sometimes confronting, and often darkly humorous, this is a story about resilience, loyalty, pride, and the lessons found in both failure and success. It captures the reality behind the chef’s jacket — the pressure, the personalities, the sacrifices, and the moments of connection that stay long after the service ends. More than a culinary journey, it is a story about rebuilding, learning, and discovering that sometimes the road to somewhere meaningful feels like the long road to nowhere while you’re on it.
readers: Someone struggling who believes nothing goes to plan or life won't get better than this moment.
Madz — the full, uncensored account of how he became her and Jacks' father, and of grief from his side.
The author — a purpose on the days it doesn't feel like there is one.
book_profile.promise: None, by design. You control nothing until you're living it; you can mitigate risk and steer toward a road worth living on, and failure is where the lessons are.
book_profile.differentiation: Competition not read by the author. Draft: a whole life, not only the career; uncensored crime and drug years; ChefTips ranked by what each lesson cost; grief from a father's side, with vulnerability shown to children as strength.
book_profile.structure: Life stage: Childhood; Pre-adolescent (father's death); Adolescent (love, loss, friendship, crime, drug use, survival); Young adult (jail, early career, mid career, first child); Adult (second child, late career, death of son, spiral into old habits and criminal circles, learning to grieve); Present day (recovery of self, making the most of life).
book_profile.title_usage: 'The Long Road To Nowhere' is used only as the book title — never as a part, chapter or section name.
book_profile.write_first: WE ARE ONLY BUT HUMAN — grief as a person, adult, father, partner and human; allowing yourself to be vulnerable, especially to children, is the strongest thing you can do for them and yourself.
book_profile.hardest_chapter: Jackson's death. Not avoided — 'it ain't ever fucken easy.'
